# Recipes

<!-- Generated by skills/core/scripts/dev_docs.py from skills/core/shared/help.json and the skill/agent frontmatter. Do not edit by hand: edit the catalog and run `dev_docs.py build`. -->

Short answers to "how do I…?". In Claude Code, ask `/dev-kit:help <question>`.

## Build a new app

1. /dev-kit:start <your idea> and answer the interview
2. /dev-kit:autopilot --until plan, then read the PRD, design and plan
3. /dev-kit:autopilot to build the rest
4. /dev-kit:status at any time

## Adopt dev-kit in an existing project

1. Commit or stash pending work, then /dev-kit:start <the change you want> in the repository root
2. Onboarding: baseline tag dev-kit-baseline, .dev/discovery.md (stack, conventions, existing docs), test baseline, ADRs discovered/imported
3. Pick the entry mode: feature (new capability), maintenance (bugs only: straight to /dev-kit:issue) or import (use the project's PRD/specs/ADRs)
4. A stage was skipped? /dev-kit:start routes to the first missing artifact; a stage that does not apply is recorded as review n/a
5. QA scores only what changed since the baseline; pre-existing problems become intangible issues

## Let it run overnight

1. Choose 'unattended with floors' in the interview, or later: /dev-kit:settings run overnight without asking
2. Cover permission prompts: /fewer-permission-prompts and --permission-mode acceptEdits
3. Run inside tmux: claude --permission-mode acceptEdits "/dev-kit:autopilot"
4. In the morning: /dev-kit:status, /dev-kit:backlog, /dev-kit:costs, /dev-kit:interview --gaps

## I found a bug

1. /dev-kit:issue "what happens and where"
2. Confirm the class the kit proposes (hotfix, current, standard, intangible)
3. Hotfix: /dev-kit:implement T-xxx → /dev-kit:qa --scope T-xxx → /dev-kit:deploy → /dev-kit:release --hotfix
4. Otherwise it waits in the queue for the next milestone's buffer or the cool-down

## I want an improvement

1. /dev-kit:issue "what should be better"
2. Standard improvements enter the next milestone's buffer; small ones the cool-down
3. See the queue with /dev-kit:backlog issues

## Change the scope (new feature, different behaviour)

1. /dev-kit:issue "the new behaviour" (class change)
2. Accept the chain prd → review prd → (ux/ui → review design) → plan replan
3. The new tasks land in future milestones; the cadence does not change

## What is left to do?

1. /dev-kit:backlog for everything pending and the recommended next step
2. /dev-kit:status for the overall picture

## How much did it cost?

1. /dev-kit:costs for this session by stage
2. /dev-kit:costs --all --by agent for the whole project
3. /dev-kit:costs --csv to apply your own prices

## Put it in production

1. Answer the production questions in the interview (method, host, when, smoke checks, prerequisites)
2. /dev-kit:deploy --check to see the drift
3. /dev-kit:deploy M3 or let autopilot deploy per milestone

## Resume after a crash or a reboot

1. /dev-kit:start to reconcile state with git
2. /dev-kit:autopilot continues from the current phase
3. /dev-kit:start also stops processes and frees locks left by the crash

## Review the session or send feedback to the author

1. /dev-kit:feedback writes a graded report and an export without project data
2. Review both files in .dev/feedback/ before sending them

## Change autonomy, quality or other settings

1. /dev-kit:settings <what you want, in words> (level, quality bar, rounds, reuse, task checks, buffer, deploys, tips)
2. /dev-kit:interview --gaps to revisit product decisions

## See progress in Claude Code itself (tips, status line, notifications)

1. /dev-kit:settings status line (or spinner tips, notifications, session title) turns each one on or off
2. Spinner tips and the status line go to .claude/settings.local.json, which stays out of git; tips show from the next session
3. After each skill, the greyed-out suggestion in the prompt is usually the next /dev-kit command: press Tab or Right arrow, then Enter

## Watch the project on a board (or share it)

1. /dev-kit:board opens the live board in the browser (one server per project)
2. /dev-kit:board --host 0.0.0.0 shares it on your network: open the access link it prints on the other device
3. /dev-kit:board stop (or the Stop server button) when done

## Ship a version

1. /dev-kit:docs all, then /dev-kit:review docs
2. /dev-kit:release --dry-run to see the checklist and the version it would use
3. /dev-kit:release (tags; pushes and deploys only as the brief allows)

## Check that the app is usable and accessible

1. /dev-kit:usability (or --url http://localhost:3000 for an app already running)
2. /dev-kit:implement to run the fix tasks it created
3. /dev-kit:usability again until review ux passes
